Dependencies are injected through the constructor as domain-defined ports (ProjectRepository, IdGenerator), so the file contains no persistence or transport logic
The check of dto.name type and emptiness is input validation at the use-case boundary and throws a domain ValidationError
The graph shows ProjectController in infrastructure handles transport and calls the use case
parsedVerdict.reasoning: CreateProjectUseCase.execute does the usual application-layer work. It checks the shape of the incoming DTO, asks the injected IdGenerator port for an id, builds a Project domain entity, saves it through the injected ProjectRepository port, and returns the result. The file has no persistence code (no SQL, ORM or file I/O), no transport or framework logic (no HTTP request or response handling and no status codes), and no infrastructure concerns. The check `typeof dto.name !== "string" || dto.name.trim() === ""` validates the type and presence of a DTO field at the use-case boundary. Validating input at that boundary is appropriate for the application layer. You could argue that "name is required" is also a Project invariant that belongs in the entity. But checking the shape of the DTO before mapping it to the entity is not a misplaced business rule. No ADR prose was given that says otherwise.
